name: simulate-batch
why: The four annual phases extracted in the simulate-batch slice, plus the sub-arms whose reach cannot be assumed. REPOINTED after the extractions landed: every range now names the extracted helper under projection/internal/, not the removed inlined block in projection/simulate.ts, and one entry (B.application) names the call site because that arm stayed there. Block D - income pass 1, wages - was REMOVED when this branch merged origin/main. That phase was extracted concurrently and independently on main as projection/internal/wageIncomeStreams.ts; this slice's duplicate helper was withdrawn rather than kept, and main's version is not this spec's to prove. The surviving ids A, B, C and E were left as they are rather than renumbered, so reach output stays comparable with the runs taken before the merge. Line numbers are against the working tree and MUST be re-checked before reuse (all sixteen were re-checked line by line during that merge and none needed correcting: the merge left the four helper files byte-identical, and in projection/simulate.ts it changed only the import block and the wages call site - the import edit is line-count-neutral, one import removed and one added, and the call site sits below the B.application range, so no range shifted) - a stale range silently reports the wrong code as reached, which is exactly what the first version of this file would have started doing the moment the first phase moved.

readingTheCounts: 'members that reach it' counts corpus members whose peak line count inside the range is non-zero. V8 block coverage splits at braces and at branch bodies, not at every statement, so a range that is straight-line code after a `continue` inherits the enclosing block's count and OVER-reports. Entries that do are marked with a note. Cold regions do not have this problem: a zero-count range is an untaken branch, exactly.
